newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq blames Iran for explosions that kills one.
newsitem.headline: Iraq blames Iran for explosions that kills one.

text.p: Iraq on Wednesday said three mortar bombs fired at the Baghdad headquarters of an Iranian opposition group killed one person and injured several others and laid blame for the attack on Tehran.

"At 10.20 p.m. (1920 GMT) yesterday night three mortar bombs were fired against the headquarters of the Iranian Mujahideen Khalq organisation near al-Andulis square in Baghdad," an Iraqi Interior Ministry source said in a statement to the Iraqi News Agency.

"The authorities concerned have started an investigation of the attack to capture the criminals and all indications show that the Iranian regime is involved in the terrorist attack," INA quoted the source, who also said one person died, as saying.

The bombs fired on Tuesday night landed a few metres (yards) from the headquarters of the Mujahideen Khalq group, which has military bases close to the border with Iran and has vowed to topple Tehran's government.

One of the mortar bombs landed in the middle of a main street wrecking a hospital laboratory while the second destroyed an Iraqi writers building. Windows of nearby buildings were shattered by the blasts.

"One patient at a nearby hospital suffered a heart attack and died at the shock of the explosions. A dozen people were injured, some of them critically with one having his leg amputated while another had his arm amputated," Hassan Nidham al-Mulki, a spokesman for the group, told reporters taken to the scene on Wednesday.
Mulki and group officials showed reporters a truck on which were three large mortars that they said fired the bombs. They said the third bomb exploded before reaching its target.
They said the truck was parked 700 metres from their headquarters and the attackers fled the area before the mortars fired with a timing device.
One of the mortar bombs caused heavy damage to the Iraqi Central Health Labratory with windows smashed, ceilings collapsed and sophisticated equipment ruined.
"Thank God the attack did not happen during office time, otherwise many of my employees would have been killed," deputy director of the laboratory, Dr Fa'iq Mohammed Hassan told Reuters on Wednesday.
"The loss in this lab is millions of dollars," he said.
The Iranian opposition, which also blamed Tehran for the attack, vowed to retaliate.
Ibrahim Zakeri, chairman of Anti-terrorism Committee of Mujahideen Khalq told a news conference the group "has the legitimate right to defend itself."
Mohammed Mohaddessin, head of foreign affairs said the group leader, Massoud Rajavi, urged the Iraqi government to prosecute the attackers and close down the Iranian embassy in Baghdad.
"Our leader has called on the Iraqi government to punish the criminals and close the Mullahs' embassy in Baghdad which is used by the regime as a nest to carry out its criminal attacks," he said.
He said Iran has mounted 43 attacks against the group headquarters and personnel in Iraq since 1993, killing at least 10 and wounding many others.
